correctness.rationale: Exact scattering amplitudes satisfy discrete two-site equations; computing flux loss gives the claimed rational law. For odd spacing its derivative is 8P/D cubed with positive denominator. The Möbius-rewritten quartic has precisely one sign change and opposite endpoint signs, so all-budget unique global interior optimum follows rigorously. Symbolic derivative/transform checks and 500 independently solved complex 4x4 scattering systems plus 180 global-budget comparisons corroborate the proof; asymptotic coefficients follow by regular root expansions. Finite tests are secondary, not universal proof.

evidence: Merkel et al. (2015) derive experimental near-perfect one-sided absorption using asymmetric side-loaded Helmholtz resonators; near-perfect absorption per se is already covered.

Longhi (2026) studies near-edge lossy sites in finite/semi-infinite arrays, with boundary reflection, CPA and transient algebraic decay under chosen initial excitation, not infinite two-port scattering with fixed sum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The new theorem does not claim the already established phenomenon of almost perfect one-sided absorption. In the inspected broader scattering and CPA work, controls are resonator detunings/couplings, boundary arrangement and drive rather than allocation of a fixed total pure onsite imaginary loss between two sites on an infinite line. Their conclusions do not imply parity-insensitive even separation and an all-budget unique odd-separation optimizer.

value.rationale: For a physically defined fixed loss budget, parity exactly separates allocation-sensitive from allocation-insensitive designs. The optimized odd-separated design approaches total absorption while same-resource single-site or even-spacing designs approach zero absorption. Global uniqueness and an exact quartic characterization eliminate optimization ambiguity and give the nontrivial impedance-matching law upstream loss tending one. This is a structural, motivated design result, not merely a numerical table or trivial reparameterization.
